correctness.rationale: For gap d between duplicate sites, cancellation gives AB=B reverse(V). Gaps 1 or 2 force a constant window; for d>=3, periodicity and the uniquely palindromic rotation of a nonconstant ternary block give the three distance-3/4/5 motifs. All larger gaps have an intermediate equal descendant; motif edges are precisely consecutive output-class edges, so count = positions minus edges. Indicator expectations yield exact formula. Standalone direct enumeration of 745596 words also validates edges and means.

originality.rationale: Two directly on-point primary full texts provide collision equations and only an upper bound for length-three and higher palindromic sphere sizes; they do not present the all-q all-n four-motif identity. Relevant capacity and code-construction papers use different invariants. Actual previously published result and accessible prior-claim comparisons show PAL2 and tandem code results that do not imply a PAL3 count. Equivalence elsewhere remains a risk.
residual_risks: A specialized derivation of the 2017 collision equations may have independently obtained this exact identity under other terminology.
Semantic search coverage and secondary indexing are necessarily incomplete; numerical experiments alone cannot establish priority.

value.rationale: Length three is the first nontrivial palindromic duplication length beyond the published exact length-one/two sphere formulas, where extra nonconstant collisions defeat run-only counting. Resolving an exact per-input q-ary sphere and mean by four local motifs provides a natural structural invariant useful in channel analysis and packing-bound calculations, not an arbitrary small-instance census.
